newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still up late on technicals, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still up late on technicals, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures held modest gains late Tuesday in sluggish trade, still underpinned by reports of stronger physical prices and some technical buying, industry sources said.
At 1400 EDT, June was still up 2.5 cents at $2.245 per million British thermal units, while July was 2.8 cents higher at $2.285. Other months were up one to 3.8 cents.

"I'd have no problems trading in a range based on the fundamentals, but there's a lot of people trading technically, and we could see more upside. At some point, it's going to come off hard," said one East Coast trader.
He said fundamentals like inventories, injections and weather were fairly neutral during the spring shoulder period.
Many traders agreed the market may be vulnerable to a sharp correction after recent gains, citing the rapid rise in open interest to record levels during this last leg up.
And some said index funds should start rolling out of length tomorrow, a factor that could pressure June with open interest in excess of 40,000 contracts.
But they said many may roll length into July, noting the still-bullish technical picture.
Weather forecasts were mixed, calling for hot temperatures in the western U.S., while the East and Midwest should range slightly below-normal.

Chart traders still pegged resistance in June at $2.28-29, then at $2.33 and the $2.385 contract high. Support was first seen at $2.20, with major buying likely at $2.05 and then along the up trendline in the $2.03 area.

In the cash, steady injection demand helped boost Gulf Coast swing prices by a couple of cents Tuesday to the low-$2.20s, with gas at Henry Hub talked in the mid-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas firmed a nickel to the low-$2.50s or better.
Early expectations for Wednesday's weekly AGA inventory report call for a build in the 25-70 bcf range versus a gain of 53 bcf a year ago.
NYMEX said 18,324 contracts traded at 1330 EDT.
On the KCBT, June was still up by four cents at $2.10, while deferreds remained steady to 3.5 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.5 cents to 14.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
